title: Evaluation of Left Ventricular Structure and Function using 3D Echocardiography
protocol: Utilize an echocardiography machine capable of 3D imaging.
Connect a 3D transthoracic echocardiography capable phased array transducer.
Apply the built-in 3-lead ECG of the ultrasound system.
Position the patient in the left lateral decubitus position.
Ensure that the ECG tracing on the screen is of good quality.
Unfreeze the image and start to examine the patient with the transducer.
Visualize a conventional apical four-chamber view.
Optimize the image quality by adjusting sector width to LV.
Lower the depth to truncate the left atrium.
Use a slight overgain.
Press the 4D button to switch to 3D mode.
Press the Multi-Slice button on the touch screen.
Acquire 3D images using Multi Beat or Single Beat mode.
Use Multi Beat mode for higher spatial and temporal resolution, reconstructing from 2, 3, 4, or 6 cardiac cycles with an end-expiratory breath-hold to minimize stitching artifacts.
Use Single Beat acquisition if modern transducers can achieve proper quality without reconstruction.
Acquire volumes at rates over 15 volumes per second for further analysis.
Freeze the image when the full-volume is reconstructed and the entire LV is visible.
Select the optimal acquired cardiac cycle(s) using Cycle Select and Number of Cycles knobs.
Press Image Store to save the selected images.
Select a 3D dataset appropriate for further analysis.
Click on Measure | Volume, and then select 4D Auto LVQ.
Modify alignment of apical slices to standard views.
Correct the apical views manually by tilting and rotation if required.
Set tilting to align the caliper with the long axis of the LV by dragging and moving the calipers on long-axis views.
Set rotation using the corresponding or Rotate All knobs on the machine or by adjusting the calipers on the short-axis image.
Click to the next step EDV after finishing view alignment.
Automatically detect the LV end-diastolic (ED) frame using the ECG signal.
Manually correct the LV end-diastolic frame if necessary.
Select two landmark points manually on any apical views.
Identify the LV apex in an apical view.
Identify the middle of the LV base (mitral annulus level) in an apical view.
Check contour credibility in three apical views.
Check contour credibility in three short-axis views of different levels.
Perform endocardial and epicardial contouring accurately and consistently.
Manually add points for contour correction as needed.
Delete previously added point using the Undo option.
Reset the contouring to start from the beginning if necessary.
Adjust contour visibility to appreciate the endocardial surface on the grey-scale image.
Choose the next step, which is the ESV.
Repeat the procedure for identifying and correcting the endocardial contour on the end-systolic frame.
Detect the end-systolic (ES) frame automatically using the ECG signal.
Manually correct the ES frame if necessary.
Press Volume waveform to proceed after values of EDV, ESV, EF, HR, SV, CO, and SpI are displayed.
View a dynamic 3D model of the LV along with the time-volume curve as it traces the endocardial surface throughout the cardiac cycle frame-by-frame.
Edit the endocardial border at any frame if necessary.
Press LV Mass to proceed to the next step after viewing the dynamic models.
Contour the LV epicardial contour on the end-diastolic frame automatically.
Calculate LV mass (EDMass) based on the contoured epicardial surface.
Edit the contour of the epicardial surface by adding points in any short- or long-axis plane if necessary.
Press 4D Strain ROI for the next step.
The software automatically contours LV epicardial contour on the end-systolic frame and calculates LV end-systolic mass (ESMass).
Edit the end-systolic contour of the epicardial surface by adding points if necessary to include any short- or long-axis plane.
Press 4D Strain Results for the next step.
The software visualizes the 3D myocardial tracking on multiple short- and long-axis planes and corresponding strain values of the 17 standard LV segments throughout the cardiac cycle, frame-by-frame.
Time-strain curves and bull's eye plot are also displayed.
Exclude a particular LV segment from analysis if it is considered as having low tracking quality based on visual observation or time-strain curve.
Visualize color-coded strain values on a dynamic 3D model of the LV by changing the "Layout".
Terminate the analysis by pressing Approve & Exit.
